1  THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED U/S 438 OF CR.P.C.,
 SEEKING TO GRANT ANTICIPATORY BAIL IN VIDYAGIRI POLICE  STATION CRIME NO.251/2022 FOR THE OFFENCE PUNISHABLE  U/S 406, 409, 420 R/W 34 OF IPC.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  CRL.P No. 100944 of 2023  ORDER Heard Sri.K.L.Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.

2. This petition is filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., with the following prayer:
"To grant anticipatory bail in Vidyagiri police station Crime No.251/2022 for the offence punishable U/s 406, 409, 420 R/w 34 of IPC"
3.

Brief facts of the case are as under:
A complaint came to be lodged by Smt.Mamata W/o Jagadish Hosagoudar, a government employee with Vidyagiri police station, Dharwad which was registered in Crime No.251/2022 on 20.12.2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
409, 420 read with 34 of IPC against Sajjan and 13 other persons.
4.

Gist of the complaint averments reveal that in respect of the compensation amount payable for the lands which were acquired by the KIADB, there was double payment made whereby there is a loss to the tune of Rs.19,99,55,000/- to the Government and petitioner and others have actively colluded in committing such fraud and therefore, sought for action.
The petitioner is shown as accused No.12 being one of the officers of the IDBI Bank, who processed the cheque.
Soon after coming to know about registration of the case, the petitioner approached the District Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

The learned II Additional and District Judge, Dharwad in Crl.Misc.
No.191/2023 by order dated 29.04.2023 rejected the anticipatory bail request.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioner is before this Court.

5. Reiterating the grounds urged in the petition, Sri.K.L.Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that at no stretch of imagination the petitioner could be a party to the alleged fraud and has colluded with the main culprit and sought for anticipatory bail.

6. He further contended that he being one of the officers of the IDBI Bank, in the usual course, has processed the cheque for encashment after following the requisite banking procedure and if the main accused has fraudulently presented the cheque for the second time for compensation amount,

sentences.text: the petitioner cannot be held responsible for the alleged fraud and sought for grant of anticipatory bail.

7. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently contended that the magnitude of fraud is huge and the amount of loss that has occurred to the KIDB is to the tune of Rs.19,99,55,000/- and without there being active collusion of the petitioner, the compensation amount could not have been disbursed and the cheque would not have been encashed and therefore,
sought for rejection of the bail.
8. She also contended that this Court taking note of the magnitude of fraud has rejected the bail for co- accused persons and therefore, sought for rejection of anticipatory bail.

9. In reply, Sri.K.L.Patil contended that rejection of bail by this Court is for the officials of KIADB who are directly involved in creating the cheque for double payment in respect of the lands which were acquired and not for the bank officials and therefore, rejection of the bail order for the officials of KIADB would not act as parity in rejecting the bail application of the petitioner.
10. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court has perused the material on record meticulously.
On such perusal, it is seen that the present petitioner is not mentioned in the FIR, but what has been shown is officials of IDBI Bank.
11. Whether at all the petitioner was involved in the alleged fraud and had colluded with the main culprit cannot be decided by this Court at this stage by holding a mini trial.

12. It is settled principles of law which requires no emphasis that the Court while deciding the bail application need not hold a mini trial to find merits or demerits of the case during the trial in one way or the other.
It is for the investigating officer to find out and unearth the truth in the alleged incident and for which custodial interrogation is necessary.
At the same time, the right of the petitioner especially when he being the bank official are also to be protected.
Admittedly, from the date of registration of the case, the petitioner is not available for the Investigating Agency and therefore, the investigation is also crippled to a considerable extent.
13. Directing the petitioner to join the investigation and to undergo limited period of custodial interrogation would meet the ends of justice.
14. Accordingly, following order is passed:

ORDER The criminal petition is allowed subject to the following conditions:
1.

The Petitioner is directed to join the investigation by appearing before the Investigating Officer on 29.05.2023 at 10.00 a.m.
2.

The Investigating Officer is at liberty to take the petitioner to custody and complete the custodial interrogation, if any, on the same day before 6.00 p.m. and thereafter Desavath Balaji Naik S/O Pere Naik vs The State Of Karnataka on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105784288/

3 enlarge the petitioner on bail by taking a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
3.

The petitioner shall co-operate with the Investigating Agency in all aspects of the matter including furnishing his handwriting specimen signature and such other queries that would be put to him by the Investigating Agency.
4. The petitioner shall attend the Court regularly.

5. The petitioner shall mark his attendance before the Investigating Officer on every 3rd Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m., till the final report is filed or a maximum period of six months whichever is earlier.
6.
The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly tamper the prosecution evidence or hamper the investigation process in any manner.
Violation of any one of the conditions would entitle the prosecution to seek for cancellation of the bail.
Ordered accordingly.
